# Satori neuron (browser app)

> The Satori neuron as a client-side web app. It registers with Satori's
> central server, polls central for the latest observation of each data
> stream, forecasts the next values with a simple model, and sends the
> predictions back to central, the way the Docker neuron (Satori Lite) does.
> It also follows Satori streams on Nostr relays and publishes a prediction
> stream (`<stream>_pred`) for each one it subscribes to, and predicts on
> Base: the vault stakes with this neuron, and its identity sends one batch
> of up/down predictions every UTC round on its own.
> Everything runs in the browser tab: the keys, the database (DuckDB-WASM on
> OPFS) and the engine. There is no server of our own. It is built to be
> driven by people and by AI agents alike.

Status: steps 1–6 of the roadmap are built (two keys, central's data flow,
the engine, Nostr, Base), a finishing pass is done, a build installs as
an app (PWA), each central stream has its own evolving multivariate
model per neuron (`bvar`) with history from central, the keys are in
this app's own format, Base only, and Home answers "is my neuron predicting
every day on its own, and is anything broken?" from an activity log, on four
tabs, phone first (2026-10-16).

Served at https://neuron.satorinet.io (https://satori.satorinet.io redirects
there; one static image; docs/design/deploy.md).

## Quick start (an agent)

In the page's JS context (Playwright's `page.evaluate`, a browser console):

1. Wait until `document.body.dataset.screen` is not `loading` (DuckDB-WASM
   and the keys take a few seconds; it is kept current: `setup`, `home`,
   `finish`, `elsewhere`, `fatal`). Then `window.satori` is ready.
2. On `setup`: `await satori.setup({ passphrase: 'at least 8 characters' })` → the
   status, `screen: 'home'`. The neuron now runs on its own.
3. `await satori.poll()`: central's observations in, predictions out.
4. `await satori.discover()`, then `await satori.subscribe(pubkey, stream_name)`
   for a free stream: each observation is forecast and published as
   `<stream>_pred`.
5. Base: fund both Base addresses (on the dev server's local fork:
   `node scripts/fork.mjs fund <identity 0x…>` and
   `node scripts/fork.mjs fund <vault 0x…> --satori 100`), then
   `await satori.unlock(passphrase)`, `await satori.stake()`,
   `await satori.predictBase()`.
6. `await satori.health()`: is it predicting, and is anything broken? Its
   `action` is the one thing to do, if any.

Every method is below; `await satori.status()` shows everything at once.

## Changed 2026-10-18 (staking: the words and the agent API)

The vault giving its prediction power to the identity (on-chain, the
vault's `delegatePredictionPower(identity)`) is called **staking**: "Stake
with this neuron", "Unstake". The old names are gone, with no aliases:

- `satori.delegate()` → `satori.stake()`, `satori.undelegate()` →
  `satori.unstake()`; the same results.
- `base()` (and `status().base`): `vault.delegated` → `vault.staked` (the
  same values: `'identity'`, `'none'`, `'other'`, null before the first
  read), `vault.delegate` → `vault.stakedWith` (the address it stakes with),
  `identity.allowedDelegator` → `identity.allowedStaker`.
- `health()`: the reason `delegate` → `stake` (and the action card's
  `data-action`), its action's `do: 'delegate'` → `do: 'stake'`, button
  "Stake", text "Your vault's SATORI isn't earning on Base. Stake with this
  neuron."; `work.task` `delegate` / `undelegate` → `stake` / `unstake`; the
  Base chip "Not staked", "Staked elsewhere", "No SATORI staked".
- `predictBase()`'s skip `no prediction power delegated to the identity` →
  `nothing staked with this neuron`.
- `data-test`: `base-delegation` → `base-staking`, `base-delegate` →
  `base-stake`, `base-undelegate` → `base-unstake`.
- Words on the page: "Delegate prediction power" / "Stop delegating" →
  "Stake with this neuron" / "Unstake" ("Staking…", "Unstaking…"); the
  Delegation fact → Staking, "Staked: 100 SATORI with this neuron" or "Not
  staked: Stake with this neuron, below"; Transfers "SATORI transfer-locked
  while delegated" → "Staked SATORI can't be sent until you unstake", and
  after Unstake "SATORI can be sent from Oct 17, 00:00 UTC (round 20743)"
  (it said "transfer-locked until round 20742 (free from …)"; `send()`
  throws the same words); the batch check "Waits until you stake"; who
  plays: "Your SATORI is staked with this neuron, so it can't also play
  Satori Daily by hand. Unstake to play manually." / "Stake with this
  neuron to let it predict every round, or play Satori Daily by hand.";
  Home's vault line "· staked"; the inline prompt "Vault passphrase to
  stake"; the transactions "Vault: stakes with this neuron" / "Vault:
  unstakes"; the feed "Staked with this neuron" / "Unstaked" (migration 10
  rewrites the log's earlier rows in these words).

## Changed 2026-10-16 (Home answers "is it predicting?"; four tabs)

For agents written against the earlier UI and API:

- New: `await satori.health()` → `{ status, title, line, action, days,
  channels, feed, reasons }` (below) and `satori.go(tab)`, `tab` one of
  `home`, `streams`, `wallet`, `settings` (also the URL's `#home` …
  `#settings`; `<body data-tab>` says which is shown). Every other method is
  unchanged.
- The page is four tabs. What moved where: the Keys card (addresses, Unlock,
  Lock), the storage line, Install and Backup → **Settings**; the Central
  card and the stream list → **Streams** (the list is open there: its
  `<details>` summary is gone, `streams-count` says how many); Nostr and
  Network streams → **Streams**; the Base card → **Wallet**; the Settings
  `<details>` → the **Settings** tab, its forms always open. Elements of a
  tab not shown are in the DOM but hidden: `go(tab)` first, or query visible
  elements.
- Unlock: Settings › Keys keeps "Vault passphrase" and `unlock`. Delegate,
  Claim, Send and Backup, asked for while locked, open one inline prompt in
  place (`unlock-prompt`, `data-unlock-for` = `card` | `claim` | `wallet` |
  `backup`, labelled "Vault passphrase to delegate", "… to claim", "… to use
  the vault", "… to back up"), then do the action. The Wallet's buttons are
  shown while locked (they were hidden until Unlock); "Unlock the vault to
  delegate, claim or send." and "Unlock the vault to back up your keys." are
  gone. The header's Lock stays (`lock`); Settings adds "Lock the vault"
  (`lock-vault`). `base-delegation` while not delegated says "Not delegated:
  Delegate prediction power, below" (it said "Unlock, then …").
- `status().central.lastPoll` may carry `local: true` (the database or the
  engine failed, not central); a failed `lastSubmit` is `{ at, error,
  total_submitted, login? }` (`login: true`: central refused the login).
- A stream row's name (`.sname`) is a button: it opens the stream's detail
  (`stream-detail`, its latest predictions as `stream-prediction`).
- `data-test` new: `home`, `health` (`data-s`: the status), `health-title`,
  `health-line`, `action` (`data-action`: the reason), `action-text`,
  `action-button`, `days` with `day` cells (`data-date`, `data-code`),
  `days-summary`, `channels` with `chip` (`data-channel`, `data-state`) and
  `chip-text`, `claimable`, `claimable-amount`, `claim`, `claim-result`,
  `home-vault`, `home-gas`, `home-stream`, `activity`, `feed`, `feed-item`
  (`data-level`), `nav-<tab>` (the computer's top nav) and `tab-<tab>` (the
  phone's tab bar), `streams-tab`, `wallet-tab`, `settings-tab`,
  `streams-count`, `stream-detail`, `stream-prediction`, `unlock-prompt`,
  `lock-vault`, `update-settings`. None removed: every earlier `data-test`
  keeps its name and meaning (`streams` is now the Streams card itself).
- Settings' sections have ids: `#settings-keys`, `#settings-backup`,
  `#settings-central`, `#settings-relays`, `#settings-base`,
  `#settings-device`.
- The database has an activity log (migration 8) and `meta.backup_at` (the
  vault's backup confirmed); docs/design/storage.md.

## Changed 2026-10-17 (latest: advice; the hero stays green)

- A reason's level (`health().reasons[].status`) may be `'advice'`: nothing
  is wrong with the neuron, but there is a good thing to do. Advice never
  changes `status`, `tone`, `title` or `line`. It is `action` only when no
  warn or bad reason is present, and it may give its channel's chip its
  words, with `state: 'advice'` and a green `tone`.
- The advice reasons: `backup` (it was `warn`: a new neuron whose storage is
  not kept and whose words were not confirmed read amber, "Central is fine.
  Back up your keys.", all through its first poll; now it is green, and the
  card offers Back up), `install` (new: the Install suggestion while *Was
  asleep*, which was `asleep`'s action; `asleep` has no action now) and
  `relay-down` (it was `warn`; the Network chip says "1 of 2 relays down",
  `state: 'advice'`).
- `reasons` are ordered by level, then as before: bad, warn, idle, advice.
  `backup` moved from after `central-failed` to after `starting`.
- `status` keeps its four values, `'ok' | 'idle' | 'warn' | 'bad'`. The
  action card's `data-tone` is `idle` (sky) for advice.

## Changed 2026-10-17 (later: what it is doing; three greens)

- `health().work`: what the neuron is doing now, or null when idle:
  `{ task, step, done, total, since, critical, text }`. `task`: `central`
  (steps `register`, `observations`, `history` with done/total streams,
  `models` with done/total targets, `send` with total predictions), `base`
  (`check`, `send`, `confirm`), `delegate` / `undelegate` / `send` (`send`,
  `confirm` with k of n, `settle`), `claim` (`rewards`, `drop`, `airdrop`,
  `confirm`), `keys` (`save`), `discover` (`ask`, relays answered), `subscribe`
  (`find`). `since`: when the step began (ms). `critical: true`: closing Satori
  now would lose work (sending predictions, a Base batch or transaction not yet
  confirmed, the keys being written); its `text` begins "Keep Satori open · ".
  `text`: the words Home shows ("Loading history · 34 of 82 streams"). The
  entry that leads is shown: a critical one first, else central, base, the
  vault's actions, keys, discover, subscribe.
- `health().tone`: the colour Home shows, alongside `status`: `'working'`
  (regular green: working as expected; starting and catching up are working),
  `'critical'` (vivid green: closing would lose work), `'idle'` (sky green:
  all good, waiting for the next cycle), `'warn'`, `'bad'` (they win), `'off'`
  (grey: only a channel deliberately not used; never the hero). Each
  `health().channels[x]` has a `tone` too (`working` while its channel has
  work in progress; `off`: Base not delegated here, or no stream subscribed).
- Home's hero (`data-test=health`): `data-tone`, `data-work` (the step it
  shows, `central:history`) and `aria-busy="true"` while working, `data-from`
  at rest: the tone it turns sky green from (over 2.5 min after work). Its line
  (`health-line`) says the step while working, then the health's line. One
  short arc turns around its ring while working, the only animation on the
  page (none with reduced motion). Chips have `data-tone`; the action card
  has `data-tone` (it had `data-s`).
- A new neuron's first poll took 17–19 s on central2 (82 streams); now about
  8 s: the poll's writes are a few set statements, central's history is
  fetched 8 at a time and written in a few commits.

## Changed 2026-10-17

- Settings → Appearance: System (default), Light, Dark, and
  `satori.setTheme(theme)`; `<html data-theme>` when not System.
- `health().channels[x].lastTraffic`: the channel's last real traffic (ms),
  or null. Home's Central, Base and Network chips glow, faintly, while their
  channel talks (`data-live` on the chip); the status's colour and icon are
  untouched.
- No start delay: a new neuron polls central at once, right after register
  (Home: *Starting*, "Getting its first predictions…"), and so does one
  reopened with a poll due ("Catching up now…"); a poll still ahead is
  kept. `status().central.nextPoll` is null until register answers. The
  health windows: 12 h of open time (was 12.5 h), the first poll within 1 h.
- `health().title` is one of `'Not predicting'`, `'Starting'`,
  `'Was asleep'`, `'Predicting'` (and `'Partly predicting'`, below), read
  from the log whichever reason leads:
  a new neuron with a vault mismatch said "Predicting" and now says
  "Starting". "Retrying", "Base is failing" and "Network is down" are gone
  (`status`, `line` and `action` say so), and "Was asleep" ends once it
  caught up.
- `health().days[].code` may be `'before'`: a day before this neuron began
  (a new neuron's strip was 13 grey "closed" days). Its cell has
  `data-code="before"` and the title "<date>: Before this neuron".
- The keys record gains `created` (unix seconds) for keys made from now on.
- `status().central.registration` gains `vault` (this vault's Base address)
  and `vault_base_address` (central's answer: the Base address it pays this
  vault's rewards to, or null). `vaultMismatch` compares the two,
  case-insensitively, and may now be `null`: unknown, a central that does
  not send `vault_base_address` (prod on `main`); that is not a mismatch.
  The mismatch text names both addresses.
- A poll forecasts each stream in its batch whose latest observation has no
  prediction made from it, not only the streams with a new row: a reload
  mid-poll (rows stored, not yet forecast) is made up by the next poll, even
  with nothing new (`lastPoll.new` 0, `predicted` > 0). An observation is
  still predicted once. Migration 9 adds `streams.predicted_ts`.
- A poll with nothing new and nothing to send reads "Up to date · next in
  9 h" (the Central chip and `health().line`; it said "0 sent just now" and
  "Polled central …, nothing new"), and "Polled central: up to date" /
  "Caught up: up to date" in the feed. "0 sent" no longer appears.
- `health().title` may be `'Partly predicting'`: central predicts, but
  Base, delegated, is red (it read a red "Predicting"). "Not predicting"
  (central) still wins; Nostr never changes the title.

## Changed 2026-10-16 (the keys in this app's own format; Base only)

For agents written against the earlier API:

- `status().identity` and `status().vault` are the keys' **Base (0x)
  addresses** (they were Evrmore "E…" addresses). No Evrmore address is
  shown or returned anywhere.
- `status().central.registration` has no `wallet_address` or
  `vault_address`; `vaultMismatch` is `false`, `'other'` (central has
  another vault for this identity) or `'none'` (it kept none).
- `setup()`: the passphrase is any Unicode, at least 8 characters (it was 4,
  Latin-1 only); a new optional `nostrKey` (nsec or hex).
- `backup('identity' | 'vault')` → `{ words, privateKey }` (`privateKey`:
  `0x` hex; it was `{ words, wif }`); new: `backup('nostr')` → `{ nsec,
  secret }` and `backup()` → all three.
- `file()` is **removed**: no Docker files (`wallet.yaml`, `vault.yaml`,
  `nostr.yaml`) are made any more. Import still reads them.
- A new screen, `finish`: an earlier version's vault whose public key was
  not in clear; `unlock(passphrase)` there finishes the update and starts
  the neuron.
- Prediction texts (`value`, `t1_value`, `observed_at`) are JS's number
  text (`100`, not `100.0`), and Nostr content is compact JSON.
- Central's login is signed with EIP-191 (Ethereum `personal_sign`) by the
  identity, as central (base-upgrade f4d72f5) and Satori Lite (satorilib
  5028913) now do; it was an Evrmore signed message. There is no Evrmore
  anywhere in the app.
- `data-test`: `identity` and `vault` now hold the Base addresses;
  `identity-base`, `vault-base`, `wif` and `download-*` are gone;
  `backup-key`, `backup-hex`, `pass-note` and `finish` are new.

## Concepts

- Base only: each key's address is its Base (0x) address, the only kind
  shown. There is no Evrmore anywhere in the app: central's login is an
  EIP-191 (`personal_sign`) signature by the identity, `0x` + r ‖ s ‖ v,
  which recovers to the identity's Base address, and register's vault check
  compares Base addresses.
- Identity key: the neuron's own key. Stored unencrypted in this browser so
  the neuron runs from page load with nobody present. It signs central's
  login challenge (EIP-191) and the daily Base batch.
- Vault key: holds funds. Stored encrypted with the passphrase
  (PBKDF2-SHA256, 600,000 rounds, and AES-256-GCM; any Unicode passphrase of
  at least 8 characters). **Unlock** (enter the passphrase) decrypts it into
  memory; **Lock** wipes it. The neuron does not need the vault to run; its
  public key is stored in clear, so its address shows while locked.
- The keys are one record of this app's own (`meta.keys`,
  docs/design/keys.md). A Dockerized Neuron's `wallet.yaml`, `vault.yaml` and
  `nostr.yaml` are imported (read and translated), never written. An earlier
  version's stored keys are carried forward: the identity and the Nostr key
  at load, the vault at its next Unlock.
- Central: `https://network.satorinet.io` in a build unless the build sets
  another (`VITE_CENTRAL_URL`; neuron.satorinet.io
  uses `https://central2.satorinet.io` for now); central2 (the dev central)
  on the dev server. Changeable (https only).
- Register: on every page load, `POST /api/v1/peer/register` with the
  identity's and the vault's public keys. Central links the vault to the
  identity once and answers `vault_base_address`, the Base address it pays
  this vault's rewards to. Another address than the vault's (or none) shows
  as a "vault mismatch" with both addresses; a central without that field
  shows none.
- Poll: `GET /api/v1/observations/batch?limit=100`, the latest observation of
  each stream (under 48 h old). The first poll runs at once, right after
  register (a new neuron, or one reopened with a poll due; no random wait),
  then every 11 h; the next time is stored, so a reload keeps it.
  `satori.poll()` (or "Poll now") runs one at once.
- Stream: one of central's streams, by uuid, with its name. Observations are
  stored once per (stream, whole second).
- History: a stream seen for the first time (and, once, every stream already
  known) gets its past from central: `GET
  /api/v1/observations/history?stream_uuid=…&limit=1000&since=<now − 1,000 h>`
  (an addition beyond the Docker neuron; central observes hourly, so ~41
  days), at most 4 calls at a time, at load and in each poll before the
  forecasts. Its rows are stored only if older than the stream's newest
  polled row, so they are never a stream's latest and never trigger a
  prediction. A central without the route (404, central2 today) is asked
  again a day later; a failure never breaks the poll.
- Prediction: made once for each stream's latest observation, from all of
  its stored history: a new row, or one a poll stored and was cut off
  before forecasting (a reload mid-poll); the next poll predicts it, even
  with nothing new (`poll.new` 0, `poll.predicted` > 0). `t1` is 12 h
  ahead, `t2` 24 h ahead (the value central scores, against the first
  observation 24 h or more after it). Sent right
  after the poll in one batch (`POST /api/v1/predictions/batch`, after a
  login signed by the identity) as `{stream_uuid, stream_name, value: t2,
  t1_value: t1, observed_at, hash}`, the numbers as JS prints them. Status
  `pending` until central accepts the batch; a rejected or failed batch is
  resent with the next poll. Pending predictions older than 22 h (2 × 11 h)
  are dropped. Every call to central is resent once on a network error, a
  timeout or a 5xx.
- Model (the engine, `src/engine/`, docs/design/engine.md): after the owner's
  `namaste_club` engine. History is cut into 12 h UTC buckets (the last value
  in each) and turned into returns r = v_k / v_(k-1) - 1 (changes
  v_k − v_(k-1) for a series with any value ≤ 0). A forecast predicts a
  stream one cadence ahead: 24 h for central (t2; t1 is 12 h).
  - `bvar` (central's streams): each target stream has its own **spec**,
    `{ companions: 1–3 other central streams, lambda1 ∈ {0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5},
    lambda2 ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 1} }`, first drawn by an RNG seeded from the
    identity's public key and the target's uuid, so every neuron starts with
    its own choice of which streams to read. The model: a Bayesian VAR(1) over
    the target and its companions (namaste_club's Minnesota prior: own lag
    variance lambda1^2, another series' (lambda1*lambda2)^2 times their
    variance ratio clipped to [0.01, 100]; noise from the OLS residuals), on
    the buckets where every series has three back-to-back values, iterated two
    12 h steps over all equations (each step clamped), then faded toward
    persistence like bar1. Its **score** is the median error of its 24 h
    forecast over the last 28 backtest origins (fit only on data up to each
    origin). After each poll one **mutation** of each spec (swap, add or drop
    a companion; move lambda1 or lambda2 one grid step), seeded by identity +
    target + generation, is scored on the same origins and kept only if it
    beats the champion's score by 5 %. `generation` counts the mutations
    proposed, `accepted` the ones kept. A companion must stay aligned with the
    target (a row shared in the target's last 4 row buckets, 7 in all): one
    that stops, or one drawn before there was history, is replaced from the
    aligned streams before the spec is scored. Specs stay in this browser
    (`model_specs`). A spec that can't fit yet (fewer than 6 + companions
    aligned rows, or a companion with no history) falls back to `bar1`, then
    `naive`; the prediction's `model` says which.
  - `bar1`: a Bayesian AR(1) on the target's own returns, r_next = phi * r.
    phi is shrunk toward 0 ("tomorrow = today") with a N(0, 0.2^2) prior:
    phi = sum(x*y) / (sum(x*x) + sigma^2 / 0.2^2). Two 12 h steps give t1 and
    t2, each step's return clamped to +-50%. Then t = last * (1 + weight *
    (growth - 1)). `weight` in [0, 1] comes from a backtest on the stream's
    own buckets (of the last 28 origins, those with three back-to-back
    buckets): weight = clamp(2 - model error / persistence error, 0, 1), so a
    model that trails the last value is faded toward it (1 with fewer than 5
    origins). The model for Nostr and Base streams.
  - `naive`: t1 = t2 = the last value. Used until a stream has 6 lag pairs.
    A pair is three back-to-back 12 h buckets, each with an observation, so
    without central's history bar1 needs an observation every 12 h (about 4
    days of polls every 11 h). A stream central updates once a day stays
    naive: gaps are not bridged.
  - `bar1d`: bar1 on changes (additive steps clamped to the largest change
    seen, absolute backtest errors) for a series with any value ≤ 0, such as
    a named Base stream's signed counter.
  `phi` (bvar: the target's own-lag coefficient) and `weight` are stored with
  each prediction (null for `naive`). `node scripts/backtest.mjs` measures
  bar1, persistence and 5 simulated bvar neurons on real history: on liquid
  crypto pairs all three tie.
- Changing the central URL drops the pending predictions, the stream list,
  the specs and the last poll/submission/history (another central has other
  stream uuids); the list refills with the next poll.

- Nostr key: a third key, random (not derived from the identity or the
  vault, so not in the 24 words), stored unencrypted like the identity. It
  signs the neuron's Nostr events; its 64-hex pubkey is sent to central on
  register (`nostr-pubkey`). Backup shows it as `nsec` and hex; Restore from
  words takes either back.
- Relays: central's list (`GET /api/v1/peer/relays`, today
  `ws://satorian.satorinet.io:7777`) plus the user's (Settings or
  `setRelays`). On the dev server central's relays are read only (requests,
  never events) and the user's relays default to the test relay
  `ws://localhost:7778`; a build writes to central's relays too, and its
  user relays default to the build's `VITE_NOSTR_RELAYS` (neuron.satorinet.io:
  `wss://app.satorinet.io/relay`). An https page
  cannot open `ws://` relays (shown as blocked); it needs `wss://`.
- Network streams: the relays' catalog of stream announcements (kind 34600),
  newest per (provider pubkey, stream name), deleted ones dropped. A
  provider is a Nostr pubkey (64 hex). Prediction streams end in `_pred`.
- Subscribe: to a free, open stream (paid, encrypted or approval-gated ones
  come later), at most `maxStreams` at once: central's `max_streams` (60
  today), or Lite's own 100 when central has not answered. It publishes a
  subscription event (34602) and announces `<stream>_pred` (34600). The
  first observation that arrives is the relays' stored latest one (an
  observation is replaceable: a relay keeps one per stream), so it may be
  old; then each new one. Each new
  observation (34601) of the stream is stored, forecast one cadence ahead
  (the engine with the stream's `cadence_seconds`, a day when it has none,
  as its step and its horizon; a forecast is one cadence ahead, the owner's
  rule) and published
  as `<stream>_pred` with `value` = the forecast as a string (`"82378.5"`),
  `seq_num` = our last + 1. A value with no number is echoed. Relay streams
  and predictions are kept apart from central's and never sent to central.
  Unsubscribe publishes the unsubscription and deletes the `_pred`
  announcement (a tombstone).
- Hourly: the relay list again, dropped relays reconnected, `_pred`
  announcements again; daily: a NIP-65 relay list (10002).

- Base (Base Sepolia, chain 84532, the D6 contracts; docs/design/base.md):
  each key's 32-byte secret is also its EVM key, so the identity and the
  vault each have a Base (0x) address (the vault's from its public key,
  stored in clear, while locked). Addresses: bundled, with central's
  `/api/v1/base/config` over them (cached 1 h; prod answers 404, central2
  serves it). RPC: Settings or `setBaseRpc`; empty = the default: on the dev
  server `/rpc`, a local anvil fork (`node scripts/fork.mjs start`); in a
  build central's (`https://sepolia.base.org`), then publicnode, unless the
  build sets `VITE_BASE_RPC`. An RPC on
  another chain than 84532 is refused (nothing is read or sent).
- Stake with this neuron (needs Unlock): on-chain, the vault's
  `hub.delegatePredictionPower(identity)`; the SATORI stays in the vault and
  earns. First the identity sets its predictor fee to 0
  (`rewards.setPredictorFee(0)`, set-once) and accepts only this vault
  (`hub.setAllowedDelegator(vault)`). Each step only when needed. Staked
  SATORI can't be sent; Unstake (`delegatePredictionPower(0x0)`) keeps it
  unsendable through the next round: the token refuses transfers while
  `transferLockedUntil >= round`, so it can be sent from round
  `transferLockedUntil + 1` at 00:00 UTC. ("Staking" in the Docker neuron
  too.)
- Automatic only: on-chain the neuron plays only through the identity's
  daily batch; manual play is Satori Daily (https://app.satorinet.io, the
  dapp). Per vault per round it is one or the other: the engine refuses a
  staked vault's own predictions (the revert `Delegated`).
- Prediction power: the vault's SATORI, staked with this neuron. A vault
  with no SATORI, or one that has not staked, gives the identity none, and
  the batch skips (`nothing staked with this neuron`).
- The daily batch (the identity, no Unlock): once per UTC round
  (`block.timestamp / 86400`), at the first check of the round (10 s after
  load, after Stake, at the round's start on the chain's clock, at least
  hourly), when the identity has staked power and no batch this round.
  Every registry stream whose binary game has voting weight (the engine pays
  only those) is forecast by the engine one cadence ahead and at least the
  24 h a round scores (horizon = max(24 h, the cadence), in n = max(1,
  floor(horizon / max(12 h, cadence))) equal steps: an hourly stream in two
  12 h steps, a 13–24 h cadence and the daily default stream in one 24 h
  step; a named stream, a signed counter, as `bar1d`); direction UP
  (payload `0x01`) if that forecast > the latest value, else DOWN (`0x02`),
  as the Docker neuron. Each game is simulated alone first (the contract's own
  checks, named games' 24 clock hours included) and only the ones that pass
  are sent, in one `engine.predictMultipleWithPayloads`, if the max fee per
  gas is within the ceiling (`setBaseMaxFee`, 2 gwei by default; above it the
  next check tries again). Its hash is kept at once, so a check never sends
  twice; the batch is stored after its receipt, its round from its block.
- Claims (needs Unlock), each on its own: `hub.claim()` when the rewards lens
  says > 0 (the vault's share of the identity's wins); the merkle drop
  (`GET /api/v1/merkle/proof/{vault}` on central, then `claimMerkle` when
  owed; the amount is what the reserve paid); the vested airdrop
  (`claimAirdrop`).
- Gas: both addresses need a little Base ETH (the identity for the batch,
  the vault for its actions). Every contract call is simulated first (a
  revert costs nothing and names the contract's error) and sent with 500,000
  gas over the estimate (unused gas is not charged); an ETH send uses its
  estimate. The tip is the node's `eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas`, the max fee
  2 × the base fee + the tip.

- The installed app (PWA; docs/design/pwa.md): a build (not the dev server)
  has a service worker that caches the page and the hashed `/assets/` (the
  app's code, DuckDB's wasm and worker), so it starts offline with its stored
  keys and data; it touches no other request (central, relays, RPC,
  `/llms.txt`). It never runs the neuron while the app is closed. The keys
  live in this origin's storage (OPFS), which a browser may clear unless it
  is persistent: the neuron asks for it (`navigator.storage.persist()`) after
  setup and on each load until it is kept. Installing helps keep it (Chrome
  grants it to installed apps; Safari keeps a Home Screen or Dock app's data).
  A Safari web app has its own storage, apart from Safari's: set it up there
  or restore it from your words. An app window and a tab share the one-tab lock.
- The database (docs/design/storage.md): every commit is checkpointed, so a
  reload or a closed tab at any moment keeps every committed write, the keys
  included. A WAL an older version left is renamed aside in OPFS (never
  deleted) before the database opens; when DuckDB could not replay it, the
  app opens anyway, as of the last checkpoint, with a notice ("Recovered the
  database: unsaved changes from the last session were set aside.") and
  `status().recovered` says the file's new name.

Times are unix seconds.

## Drive it from the page (window.satori)

Open the app and wait until `document.body.dataset.screen` is not `loading`
(synchronous, kept current; `await satori.status()` says the same). Then, in
the page's JS context:

- `await satori.status()` → `{ screen, identity, vault, unlocked, central, nostr, base, storage, app, recovered }`.
  `screen` is `setup` (no keys yet), `home` (running), `finish` (an earlier
  version's vault whose public key was not in clear: `unlock(passphrase)`
  once, then it runs), `elsewhere` (another tab has it open; only one tab
  runs the neuron) or `fatal`. `identity` and `vault` are the keys' Base
  (0x) addresses (null before setup). `central` (on
  `home`) is `{ url, registration, lastPoll, nextPoll, polling, lastSubmit,
  pending, history }`:
  - `registration`: null while registering; then
    `{ at, ok: true, peer_id, message, vault, vault_base_address,
    vaultMismatch }` or `{ at, ok: false, error }` (central refused or is
    unreachable). `vault`: this vault's Base address; `vault_base_address`:
    central's answer, the Base address it pays this vault's rewards to (null
    when it has none, or does not say). `vaultMismatch`: `false` (the same
    address, in any letter case), `'other'` (a different one), `'none'`
    (central has no vault for this identity) or `null` (unknown: a central
    without the field, as prod on `main`; not a mismatch).
  - `lastPoll`: `{ at, streams, new, predicted, engine_ms }` or `{ at, error }`
    (central's error, or a local one such as a database write, then with
    `local: true`); `engine_ms`: how long the models took (present when a
    stream was forecast).
  - `history`: the last history run `{ at, url, streams, rows, left, error,
    retryAt }` (`retryAt`: the route 404'd, asked again then) and `needed`,
    how many streams have no history yet.
  - `lastSubmit`: `{ at, total_submitted, successful, failed, errors }` or
    `{ at, error, total_submitted }` (with `login: true` when central refused
    the login); `pending`: how many predictions wait to be sent.

  `storage` and `app` are there on every screen. `storage`: `{ persisted,
  usage, quota }` (`persisted`: the browser keeps this origin's data, the keys
  included, under storage pressure; `usage` and `quota` in bytes, null if the
  browser does not say). `app`: `{ installed, canInstall, update }`
  (`installed`: running as an installed app, or installed from this page;
  `canInstall`: Chromium offered its install prompt; `update`: a new version
  is waiting, see `update()`). `recovered`: null, or the name a WAL DuckDB
  could not replay was set aside under at this page load
  (`satori-mvp.duckdb.wal.unreplayed-<time>`; its changes are not in the
  database; the keys are, as setup checkpoints them). `fatal`: the screen
  shows the error; nothing was deleted, and a reload tries again.
- `await satori.health()` → Home's answer, read fresh (docs/design/health.md):
  `{ status, tone, title, line, action, days, channels, feed, reasons, work }`.
  - `tone`: `'idle'` (sky green, all good at rest), `'working'`,
    `'critical'` (keep Satori open), `'warn'`, `'bad'`; `'off'` only for a
    channel (below).
  - `work`: null, or what the neuron is doing now: `{ task, step, done,
    total, since, critical, text }` (the changelog above lists the steps).
  - `status`: `'ok'` (predicting: central took predictions within 12 h of
    open time, and if staked Base has this round's batch or its check has
    not run yet), `'idle'` (calm: *Starting* before the first poll, or *Was
    asleep*: a poll came due while Satori was closed; it catches up and says
    so until the next normal cycle; never red for being closed), `'warn'`
    (predicting, but something needs the person) or `'bad'` (predictions are
    failing).
  - `title`: is the neuron predicting on the channels that pay (central,
    and Base when it should be), whichever reason leads the status and the
    action; the first that holds: `'Not predicting'` (a bad central reason:
    `db-error`, `login-refused`, `central-failing`, `central-overdue`),
    `'Partly predicting'` (central predicts, but Base has a red reason,
    `base-failing`, while it is staked with this neuron, or not read
    after a batch went out), `'Starting'` (no good cycle in the log yet),
    `'Was asleep'` (a session missed work and has not caught up), else
    `'Predicting'`. Nostr never changes it.
  - `line`: the top reason's words (advice has none), or with none "Sent 83
    predictions 2 h ago · next in 9 h" ("Up to date · next in 9 h" when the
    last poll had nothing to send).
  - `action`: null, or the one thing to do, the highest reason with a
    button (so advice only when no warn or bad reason is present): `{ id,
    text, button, do, tab?, section? }`, `do` one of `reload`, `poll` (`satori.poll()`), `stake`
    (`unlock()` then `stake()`), `backup` (`unlock()` then
    `backup('vault')`), `install` (`install()`), `go` (`go(tab)`; the fix is
    at `#<tab>-<section>`).
  - `reasons`: every reason, highest first: `[{ id, status, channel, text }]`,
    `status` the reason's level: `'bad'`, `'warn'` (something is wrong for
    predicting or earning), `'idle'` (a calm state) or `'advice'` (nothing
    is wrong: a suggestion, the card only; it never moves `status`, `tone`,
    `title` or `line`). The order, by level: bad `db-error`,
    `login-refused`, `central-failing` (2 cycles failed), `central-overdue`,
    `base-failing`, `relays-down`; warn `central-failed` (1 cycle),
    `vault-mismatch`, `not-registered`, `stake` (the vault holds SATORI,
    not staked), `gas-low`, `base-skipped`, `base-unreachable`; idle
    `asleep`, `starting`; advice `backup` (storage not kept, no backup
    confirmed), `install` (was asleep, and the browser offers Install),
    `relay-down` (some relay down, not all). docs/design/health.md says why
    each has its level.
  - `days`: the last 30 local days, oldest first: `{ date: 'YYYY-MM-DD',
    code: 'full' | 'part' | 'error' | 'closed' | 'before', ran, today }`
    (full: predictions went out on every channel active that day; part:
    some; error: only failures; closed: nothing went out and nothing failed,
    `ran` says whether the app ran; before: the day ended before this neuron
    began, its first session or its keys' creation: not a closed day, and
    not counted in `days-summary`, "1 full day", "2 of 3 full days"). The
    phone shows the last 14.
  - `channels`: `{ central, base, network }`, each `{ state: 'ok' | 'warn' |
    'bad' | 'idle' | 'advice', tone, text, lastTraffic }` (`tone`: `working`, `idle`,
    `off`, `warn`, `bad`) ("83 sent 2 h ago", "Up to date ·
    next in 9 h" (nothing to send), "Round 20742
    sent", "No streams"); `lastTraffic`: when that channel last had real
    traffic (a request to central or its answer, a Base RPC call or its
    answer, a relay message sent or received), ms since the epoch, or null.
    Home's chip glows while it is recent (`data-live`).
  - `feed`: the activity log, newest first, 20: `{ at, level, text }`.
- `satori.setTheme(theme)` → the theme: `'system'` (the default: the
  device's light or dark), `'light'` or `'dark'`, as Settings → Appearance;
  kept on this device (localStorage, read before the first paint) and set as
  `<html data-theme>` (none for System). Anything else throws.
- `satori.go(tab)` → the tab: shows `home`, `streams`, `wallet` or `settings`
  (a leading `#` is fine), as the nav does. Anything else throws.
- `await satori.install()` → `'accepted' | 'dismissed' | 'unavailable'`: the
  browser's install prompt when `status().app.canInstall` (Chromium only; it
  needs a user gesture, which Playwright's `page.evaluate` provides; a person
  answers it). `'unavailable'` when there is none (installed, Safari,
  Firefox, an incognito window such as Playwright's default context, or not
  offered yet).
- `satori.update()` → true, then the page reloads into the new version, when
  `status().app.update`; false when none is waiting. Never automatic.
- `await satori.setup({ passphrase, vaultWords?, identityWords?, nostrKey? })` → status.
  Creates the neuron on a fresh browser (random keys unless 24 words, or the
  Nostr key's nsec or hex, are given). Passphrase: any Unicode, at least 8
  characters (code points after NFC). The vault starts locked. One setup runs at
  a time: a call while another (or the UI's) is running throws `Busy (setup)…`,
  and a call once set up throws `Already set up`.
- `await satori.poll()` → `{ poll, submit }`: poll central now, store, forecast
  each stream in the batch whose latest observation has no prediction yet
  (a new row, or one an interrupted poll stored), and send everything pending. `submit` is null
  when nothing was pending or when the poll failed (`poll.error`). It never
  throws for central's errors. One poll runs at a time; a call during one
  returns it. The next poll is then 11 h later.
- `await satori.streams()` → one row per stream: `uuid`, `name`, `meta`
  (central's stream meta: the parsed object when it is JSON, else its text,
  or null), `observations`, `obs_ts`, `obs_value`, and our latest `t1`, `t2`,
  `model` (`bvar`, `bar1`, `bar1d` or `naive`), `phi`, `weight`, `made_at`,
  `status` (`pending`/`sent`), `sent_at`; the stream's `spec` (`{ companions:
  [uuid], lambda1, lambda2 }` or null), `score`, `generation`, `accepted`; and
  `history_at` (when its history came from central; null: not yet).
- `await satori.models()` → each target's champion spec: `[{ uuid, name,
  model, spec: { companions: [{ uuid, name }], lambda1, lambda2 }, score,
  generation, accepted }]` (`model`: what made its latest prediction; `score`:
  the median relative error of its 24 h forecast over its last 28 backtest
  origins, null below 5).
- `await satori.predictions(stream, limit = 20)` → one stream's predictions
  (by uuid or name), newest first: `[{ id, stream_uuid, name, made_at, model,
  t1, t2, phi, weight, observed_at, hash, status, sent_at }]`. `observed_at`
  and `hash` are what was sent: as in Lite, `observed_at` is the time the
  prediction was made (unix seconds as JS prints them), not the
  observation's time; `hash` = sha256(value + observed_at)[:16].
- `await satori.setCentral(url)` → `status().central`: an https URL, or `''`
  for the default; registers there at once. A different URL drops the pending
  predictions and the stream list (see Concepts).
- `await satori.unlock(passphrase)` → true (one at a time, as the UI's:
  another while one runs throws `Busy (unlock)…`); `satori.lock()` → true.
  An earlier version's vault is re-encrypted in this app's format at its
  first Unlock (same passphrase). On the `finish` screen it also starts the
  neuron.
- While unlocked: `satori.backup('identity' | 'vault')` → `{ words,
  privateKey }` (the 24 words; `privateKey` is `0x` and 64 hex, what a Base
  wallet's "Import account" takes: the words follow satorilib's scheme, so a
  standard wallet derives another account from them);
  `satori.backup('nostr')` → `{ nsec, secret }`; `satori.backup()` → `{
  identity, vault, nostr }`. Any other name throws. Backup needs Unlock as
  Docker's dashboard needs login, the identity and the Nostr key too,
  although they are stored unencrypted: they are private keys. (`file()` is
  gone: no Docker files are made.)
- `await satori.nostr()` (also `status().nostr`) → `{ pubkey, npub,
  maxStreams, centralWrite, userRelays, relays, subscriptions }`. `relays`:
  `[{ url, from: ['central' | 'user'], write, state, error }]`, state
  `open` | `connecting` | `closed` (it retries) | `blocked`. `subscriptions`:
  `[{ uuid, stream, provider, name, cadence_seconds, subscribed_at,
  observations, observation: { seq, ts, value, raw, received_at } | null,
  prediction: { stream, seq, value, model, made_at, relays } | null }]`
  (`value` is the number taken from the observation or null; `raw` is what
  the provider sent; `prediction.relays` is how many relays took our latest
  `_pred`; `model` is `bar1`, `bar1d`, `naive` or `echo`). `maxStreams` is
  100 until central's relay config answers, then central's (60).
- `await satori.discover()` → the catalog: `[{ pubkey, stream_name, name,
  description, cadence_seconds, price_per_obs, encrypted, approval_required,
  tags, metadata, created_at, pred, subscribed, relays }]`, newest first;
  `relays` lists the relays that sent the announcement. Right after
  a load it waits up to 10 s for the relays still connecting, then throws if
  none is open.
- `await satori.subscribe(pubkey, stream_name)` → the subscription (as in
  `nostr().subscriptions`). Throws for a `_pred` stream, one no connected
  relay announces, a paid/encrypted/gated one, or over `maxStreams`. Again on
  a subscribed stream: returns it.
- `await satori.unsubscribe(pubkey, stream_name)` → `nostr()` (as `setRelays`).
- `await satori.relayPredictions(pubkey, stream_name, limit = 20)` → our
  `<stream>_pred` history for that stream, newest first: `[{ seq, value,
  model, obs_seq, made_at, event_id, relays }]` (`relays`: how many relays
  took it; 0 until they answer).
- `await satori.setRelays({ relays?: ['wss://…'], centralWrite?: boolean })`
  → `nostr()`: the user's relays (ws:// or wss://; they replace the list) and
  whether central's relays are written to.
- `await satori.base()` (also `status().base`, without the fresh read) → `{ rpc: ['/rpc'],
  rpcSetting, localFork, explorer, maxFeeSetting, maxFeeGwei, config: 'central' | 'bundled', error, errors, round, chainTime,
  identity: { address, eth, power, fee, allowedStaker, batchesLeft, lowEth },
  vault: { address, eth, satori, stakedWith, staked: 'identity' | 'none' | 'other',
  lock: { locked, indefinite, untilRound, freeAt } }, claimable: { rewards, airdrop },
  lastBatch: { round, at, hash, games: [{ streamId, gameId, named, direction, model, latest, forecast, horizon }],
  dropped: [{ …, error }] } | null, lastCheck, nextCheck, checking }`. Amounts
  are decimal strings (ETH, SATORI); `fee` is in basis points (1000 = the
  10 % default); `direction` 1 = UP, 2 = DOWN; a game's `latest` is the
  registry's last value (an `int232` in the stream's own units: the default
  stream, id 1, is the capital deployed in predictions ÷ the supply × 1e18)
  and `forecast` the engine's at `horizon` seconds ahead, in the same units,
  rounded, both as decimal strings (they pass 2^53; a batch stored before the
  horizon rule has `t2` instead); `lastCheck` is the last batch check:
  `{ at, round, sent }`, `{ at, round, skipped }` or `{ at, error }`.
  `rpcSetting` and `maxFeeSetting` are what Settings stored (`''` and null:
  the defaults); `maxFeeGwei` is the ceiling in force. Before the first
  chain read (a second or two after load) `status().base` has `rpc: []`,
  `config: null` and null chain values; `satori.base()` reads at once.
- `await satori.stake()` (needs Unlock): stake with this neuron → `{ steps: [{ step, by: 'identity' | 'vault', hash }], settled }`.
  `steps` is empty when everything was in place.
- `await satori.unstake()` (needs Unlock) → the same shape.
- `await satori.predictBase()` → the batch now, if due: `{ at, round, sent: { round, at, hash, games, dropped } }`
  or `{ …, skipped: 'already predicted this round' | 'nothing staked with this neuron' |
  'gas above the ceiling: …' | 'waiting for the batch already sent (0x…)' | … }` or `{ at, error }`.
- `await satori.claim()` (needs Unlock) → `{ rewards, merkle, airdrop }`, each
  `{ hash, amount }`, `{ skipped: why }` or `{ error }`.
- `await satori.send({ asset: 'ETH' | 'SATORI', to: '0x…', amount: '1.5' })`
  (needs Unlock) → `{ hash }`, from the vault. SATORI that can't be sent
  (staked, or through the round after Unstake) throws, saying when it can.
- `await satori.setBaseRpc(url)` → `base()`: an https URL, a path on this
  site (such as `/rpc`), or `''` for the default. A saved URL replaces the
  default.
- `await satori.setBaseMaxFee(gwei)` → `base()`: the batch's ceiling on the
  max fee per gas (a positive number; `''` or null = 2 gwei). Settings saves
  both at once and checks both before saving either.

Errors are thrown as `Error` with a readable message (for example
`Wrong passphrase`, `Unlock the vault first`). Central's errors are not
thrown: they are in `status().central` (for example `central 500: …`,
`central unreachable: Failed to fetch`, `central timed out (15 s)`).

## Drive it from the UI

- Setup: "Create a new neuron" (shows the vault's 24 words, asks for three of
  them, then a passphrase), "Restore from words" (vault words, optional
  identity words, an optional Nostr key as nsec or hex), or "Import
  Dockerized Neuron files" (`wallet.yaml`, `vault.yaml`, optional
  `nostr.yaml`, the vault password, and "Use it as this app's passphrase
  too", ticked: when the Docker password is shorter than 8 characters, or
  unticked, the passphrase step asks for a new one). `wallet.yaml` is the
  unencrypted file and `vault.yaml` the encrypted one; files in the wrong
  slots, or a vault.yaml that is not encrypted, are refused with a message
  saying so. The files' keys are stored in this app's own format; the files
  are not kept.
- "Unlock to finish the update" (screen `finish`): the vault passphrase
  field ("Vault passphrase to finish the update") and Unlock.
- Four tabs once set up: a tab bar at the bottom on a phone, a top nav on a
  computer (1024 px and wider); the URL's `#home`, `#streams`, `#wallet`,
  `#settings` open them (a link or a reload keeps the tab). The header has
  Lock while unlocked and "Update ready, reload" when a new version waits.
- **Home** answers "is my neuron predicting every day on its own, and is
  anything broken?" at a glance (`health()`'s object, drawn): the health (an
  icon and a color: green while all is well, sky at rest, regular while
  working, vivid while it must stay open; amber for warn, red for bad; the
  title and one line), at most one action card (its text and one button that
  does the thing or goes there, amber or red for a problem, sky for advice;
  when it needs the vault, the passphrase is asked in place), the last 14 days (30 on a computer, with a legend: full, part of
  the day, closed, error; today outlined), the Central, Base and Network
  chips (each opens its tab), and the claimable rewards with Claim (the
  vault's SATORI, staked or not, under it). On a computer it is a
  dashboard: also the first 8 streams (latest, forecast 24 h, model with its
  companions, a trend line of the last 24 observations) with a link to all,
  the wallet (claimable, the vault, the identity's gas in days) and the
  activity feed (open; a tap away on a phone).
- **Streams**: the **Central** card (the URL, Registered, Last poll, Next
  poll, Last submission, Pending, History, a vault mismatch if any, "Poll
  now"); the **Streams** card ("N from central, with our forecasts"; one row
  per stream: latest value and time, t1, t2, the model with its spec's
  companions, "bvar · +eth +gold", or "naive · spec +eth" while the spec waits
  for aligned rows, with λ1, λ2, phi, weight, generation and score in its
  hover title, Sent/Pending; a tap on the name opens its detail: the trend,
  the model in words, its latest predictions); **Nostr** (each relay with its
  state, "Connected · read only"; each subscribed stream: latest value and
  time, our `_pred` value, its seq, how many relays took it, Unsubscribe);
  **Network streams** (opening it discovers): a search box and the first 50
  matching streams with Subscribe/Unsubscribe.
- **Wallet**: the **Base** card: the round, the vault's SATORI and ETH,
  Claimable, Staking ("Staked: 100 SATORI with this neuron"), Transfers
  ("Staked SATORI can't be sent until you unstake", "SATORI can be sent from
  <date> (round N)", "Free to send"), the identity's ETH as daily batches of
  gas (a low warning once staked), Last batch, Batch check, the RPC, who
  plays (this neuron, or Satori Daily by hand, linked), then "Stake with
  this neuron" or "Unstake", "Claim", and a send form
  (asset, Amount, "To (0x address)", "Send from the vault"); while locked
  each asks for the passphrase in place ("Vault passphrase to use the
  vault"), then does it.
- **Settings**: **Keys** (each key with Copy: the identity's Base address,
  the vault's with its Locked/Unlocked badge, the "Vault passphrase" field
  and Unlock, or "Lock the vault"; the Nostr pubkey), **Backup** (Identity
  words, Vault words, each with its private key in 0x hex; Nostr key, nsec
  and hex; asked for while locked, the passphrase in place; no downloads),
  **Central** (URL, empty = default; Save), **Nostr relays** (one per line,
  "Publish to central's relays"; Save relays), **Base** (Base RPC, "Daily
  batch: max fee (gwei)"; Save Base settings), **This device** (the storage
  line, "Storage: kept", or "Storage: the browser may clear it; install
  Satori or back up your words", with the usage of the quota; **Install
  Satori** when the browser offers it, or Safari's way to add it; the
  version, and "Update ready, reload" when one waits). Setup shows Install
  too.
- Every screen and tab is built once and shown or hidden (the `hidden`
  attribute), so Setup's labels and other tabs' elements stay in the DOM:
  query visible elements, use `data-test`, or `go(tab)` first.
- Form fields have labels; elements carrying data or actions have
  `data-test` attributes. Home: `home`, `health` (`data-s` = the status,
  `data-tone`, `data-work` and `aria-busy` while working, `data-from` at rest),
  `health-title`, `health-line`, `action` (`data-action` = the reason),
  `action-text`, `action-button`, `days` with `day` (`data-date`,
  `data-code`), `days-summary`, `channels` with `chip` (`data-channel`,
  `data-state`, and `data-live` while its channel has traffic: until 1.5 s
  after the last, 3 s with reduced motion) and `chip-text`, `claimable` with `claimable-amount`, `claim`
  and `claim-result`, `home-vault`, `home-gas`, `home-stream`, `activity`,
  `feed` with `feed-item` (`data-level`). Tabs: `nav-<tab>`, `tab-<tab>`,
  `streams-tab`, `wallet-tab`, `settings-tab`. Streams: `central-url`,
  `registered`, `last-poll`, `next-poll`, `last-submit`, `pending`,
  `history`, `mismatch`, `poll-now`, `streams` (the card) with
  `streams-count` and `stream` rows (`obs`, `t1`, `t2`, `model`, `status`
  inside), `stream-detail` with `stream-prediction`, `relay` (with
  `relay-state`), `sub` (a subscribed stream, with `sub-obs`, `sub-pred`,
  `sub-seq`, `sub-relays`, `unsubscribe`), `network`, `catalog-summary` and
  `catalog-row` (with `catalog-action`: Subscribe or Unsubscribe). Wallet:
  `base-refresh`, `base-rpc`, `base-error`, `base-identity`, `base-vault`,
  `base-staking`, `base-play` (who plays: this neuron or Satori Daily),
  `base-lock`, `base-claimable`, `base-last-batch`, `base-check`,
  `base-stake`, `base-unstake`, `base-claim`, `base-result`,
  `base-txs` (the last action's transactions), `base-action-error`.
  Settings: `identity`, `vault` (the Base addresses), `vault-state`,
  `nostr-pubkey`, `unlock`, `lock-vault`, `backup-key` (a private key, or
  the nsec), `backup-hex` (the Nostr key's hex), `theme-system`,
  `theme-light`, `theme-dark` (Appearance, `aria-pressed` on the chosen
  one), `storage`, `install`, `install-hint`, `update-settings`. The inline prompt: `unlock-prompt`
  (`data-unlock-for`). Elsewhere: `lock`, `update` (the header), `finish`,
  `pass-note`, `notice` (the recovered database's, with Dismiss) and `fatal`
  (the error that stopped the start).

## Base on the dev server: the local fork

The dev server's default Base RPC is `/rpc`, which it proxies to an anvil
fork of Base Sepolia on 127.0.0.1:8545 (the real D6 contracts; nothing goes
to a public chain). `node scripts/fork.mjs --help` lists:

- `start` / `stop` (anvil in the background, 2 s blocks; needs Foundry's
  anvil), every command taking `--port 8545`;
- `fund <0x…> [<0x…> …] [--eth 0.1] [--satori N]`: each address gets the ETH
  (0.1 by default) and, only with `--satori`, N SATORI from the deployer
  (~519 in all);
- `airdrop <0x…> <SATORI>`, `merkle <0x…> <SATORI>` (prints the proof a stub
  central serves), `advance [days]` (chain time; then `predictBase()`),
  `predict [up|down]` (moves the default stream), `stream [name]` (a game
  with no voting weight, which the batch leaves out).

Recipe: `fund <identity 0x…>` (gas for the batch) and
`fund <vault 0x…> --satori 100` (gas and SATORI to stake), then
Unlock, `stake()`, `predictBase()`.

## From the Docker neuron (migrate in, never back)

The keys are Satori Lite's (github.com/SatoriNetwork/satori-lite and
github.com/SatoriNetwork/satorilib): one
32-byte secp256k1 secret per key = the private key = the BIP39 entropy of its
24 words. A Dockerized Neuron moves here by Import (its `wallet.yaml`,
`vault.yaml` with the vault password, and `nostr.yaml`) or by Restore from
words; its keys are then stored in this app's own format. Nothing is written
back in Docker's formats. Central sees the same identity either way, and on
Base the same secrets give the same 0x addresses as the Docker neuron's
(`ethAddress`), so the stake and rewards follow the keys. Satori Lite is the
reference for what goes over the network: central's payload and Satori's
Nostr events carry Lite's fields (the text as JS writes it: numbers like
`100`, compact JSON, which central and satorilib parse; see
docs/design/central.md and nostr.md, "The protocol audit").

## Code

Repository: https://github.com/lastmeta/Satori (this app is the repository
root; branch `main`). Plain JavaScript ES modules, no
build step beyond Vite, MIT licensed.

- `src/main.js`: app wiring and `window.satori`; `src/config.js`: Settings'
  defaults, the dev server's or a build's, each replaced by a `VITE_*`
  variable at build time (`VITE_CENTRAL_URL`, `VITE_NOSTR_RELAYS`,
  `VITE_NOSTR_CENTRAL_WRITE`, `VITE_BASE_RPC`); `src/util.js`: `serial()`
  (one at a time, in order), `isHttps()` and `isRelayUrl()`.
- `src/keys/`: the keys record (`index.js`: create, import, migrate, load,
  Unlock), the vault encryption and the passphrase rule (`vault.js`), a
  key's words, public key, Base address and signatures (`keys.js`), Docker's
  files read for import and migration (`docker.js`).
- `src/central/`: central's API (register, observations, login, predictions
  batch); `login.js`: central's login signature, EIP-191 by the identity.
- `src/db/`: DuckDB-WASM on OPFS, schema migrations, small async API; every
  commit checkpointed; `recover.js` sets aside a WAL an older version left.
- `src/engine/`: `forecast(points, { step, horizon }) → { model, t1, t2, value,
  horizon, phi?, weight? } | null`, pure: `step` is the bucket in seconds (12 h
  by default; a relay stream's cadence), `horizon` how far ahead `value` is
  (two steps by default; a forecast is one cadence ahead: 24 h for central,
  where value = t2; one cadence for a relay stream; max(24 h, cadence) on
  Base); t1 and t2 are one and two steps ahead; `{ weight }` forces the fade.
  `bvar.js`: the Bayesian VAR(1) of a target and its companions, its backtest
  and fallbacks; `evolve.js`: `runModels({ fresh, histories, specs, seed })`,
  each target's identity-seeded spec, one mutation per poll, the forecasts.
- `src/nostr/`: NIP-01 events and the Nostr key over `@noble/curves`
  (`event.js`), Satori's events and parsing (`satori.js`), one relay over a
  WebSocket with reconnect (`relay.js`).
- `src/traffic.js`: `emit(channel)` on every request and answer (central's
  fetch, Base's RPC transport, each relay message) and `subscribe(fn)`:
  Home's glow (`src/ui/glow.js`) and `lastTraffic`.
- `src/neuron/`: register, the cycle (poll → store → history → forecast →
  submit), `history.js` (central's history for new streams), central's status, the schedule (`schedule.js`, shared with Base), the
  one-tab lock; `nostr.js`: relays, discover, subscribe, intake → `_pred`,
  reconcile; `base.js`: the daily batch and its schedule, stake, claims,
  sends, the Base settings; `activity.js`: the activity log (sessions,
  cycles, checks, publishes; 90 days); `health.js`: Home's answer from it,
  pure (`health()`), with its tone; `work.js`: what it is doing now
  (`health().work`).
- `src/chain/`: Base over viem: `config.js` (addresses, RPC), `abi.js`,
  `index.js` (`createChain`: status multicall, stake, the batch's pieces,
  claims, sends).
- `src/ui/`: ArrowJS: `view.js` (the shell, the tabs, Setup and the screens
  before Home), `home.js`, `streams.js`, `wallet.js`, `settings.js`,
  `parts.js` (the inline Unlock, shared pieces), `state.js`, `format.js`,
  `glow.js` (the chips' traffic glow), `hold.js` (the pace of the hero's
  steps), `theme.js` (Appearance;
  `public/theme.js` applies it before the first paint); `src/style.css` (the
  tokens: light, dark by the system, dark when chosen).
- `src/pwa/`: the installed app: `sw.js` (the service worker; a build writes
  it to `dist/sw.js` with the files to precache, `vite.config.js`) and
  `index.js` (register it in a build, Update, Install, persistent storage);
  `public/manifest.webmanifest` and the icons.
- `deploy/`: the static image (nginx serving `dist/` behind central's
  nginx-proxy, which terminates TLS): `Dockerfile`, `nginx.conf` (the CSP
  from `csp.js` on every response, cache headers, the SPA fallback) and
  `build.env` (the deployment's `VITE_*`); `scripts/deploy-image.sh` builds
  and checks `satori-neuron:<git sha>`.
- `docs/design/`: what is built and why (`OVERVIEW.md`, `health.md` (Home's
  rules: thresholds and the action priority; `home-mockup.html` the approved
  design), `keys.md`,
  `central.md` with Satori Lite's file:line references, `engine.md` with
  namaste_club's, the deviations and the backtest numbers, `nostr.md` with
  Lite's and satorilib's, `base.md` with Lite's, the dapp's and the
  contracts', `storage.md`: tables, migrations, meta keys, the checkpoint rule and recovery, `pwa.md`: the
  installed app, `deploy.md`: the image and the build variables); `docs/plans/`:
  the roadmap and what is left of each part; `docs/issues/`: open issues
  outside this repo; `docs/inbox/QUESTIONS.md`: open questions for the
  owner.
- `scripts/`: parity-vector generators run against satorilib and
  namaste_club (Python; `bvar_parity.py` for bvar), and
  `profile_fixtures.mjs` (the keys each earlier version stored); `backtest.mjs`
  (node, read only: bar1, persistence and simulated bvar neurons);
  `test-relay.mjs` (an in-memory Nostr relay: `node scripts/test-relay.mjs
  7778`) and `provider.mjs` (a throwaway stream provider for a test relay);
  `fork.mjs` (the local fork of Base Sepolia, above); `deploy-image.sh` (the
  deploy image).
- `test/`: fixtures (parity vectors) and test doubles (a fake D6 behind
  JSON-RPC, an in-memory DuckDB); `e2e/`: Playwright specs and their stub
  central (`stub.js`).
- Tests: `npm test` (vitest), `npm run e2e` (Playwright, Chrome, a stub
  central, two test relays, a fake chain behind `/rpc`), `npm run e2e:pwa`
  (a build on `vite preview` :5181: the manifest, the service worker,
  offline, Update, one neuron), `npm run e2e:deploy` (the deploy image at
  `DEPLOY_URL`: headers on every response, then the app in a fresh profile).

## Contribute

Pull requests are welcome at https://github.com/lastmeta/Satori. Keep changes
small, tested (vitest / Playwright) and in plain JS; follow the patterns of the
Docker neuron (Satori Lite) and satorilib; update `docs/design/` and this file
with what you change.
